sentenceSets.sentence: The researcher argued that the brain's filing system is analogous to a library's cataloguing method.

answerChoices.reasoning: Identical means exactly the same; while analogous indicates comparison, it specifies similarity in function, not that the brain and library are identical.
Superior means greater in quality or rank; an analogy compares functioning, not making value judgments about which system is better.
Derived means originating from; while the brain's system might have inspired library methods, analogy refers to functional similarity, not derivation.
Equivalent means equal in value; while analogous items are similar, they need not be equivalent in all respects.
Opposite means contrary or reverse; an analogy between the brain and library suggests similarity in function, not opposition.
Independent means not dependent on; an analogy suggests a relationship of comparison, not independence.
Unrelated means having no connection; an analogy specifically proposes a meaningful similarity or comparison.
Invented means created originally; an analogy compares existing systems, not crediting creation to one entity.
Contradictory means logically opposed; an analogy suggests functional similarity, not contradiction.
Proven means established as true; an analogy is a comparison used to illustrate, not proof of equivalence.
Incompatible means unable to work together; an analogy suggests similarity in function, not incompatibility.

sentenceSets.sentence: The legal team drew an analogy to a historical precedent that was analogous to the current case in several important ways.

answerChoices.reasoning: Contradicted means opposed or negated; finding a precedent analogous to the current case suggests reinforcement, not contradiction.
Opposite means contrary; an analogy requires similarity between precedent and current case, not opposition.
Irrelevant means not applying or not connected; an analogous precedent is directly relevant to the current case.
Inconsistent means not in agreement; a precedent analogous to the current case shows consistency in important ways.
Disconnected means having no link; an analogous precedent shows important connections to the current case.
Unrelated means having no connection; an analogous precedent has important similarities to the current case.
Incomparable means impossible to compare meaningfully; an analogous precedent can be meaningfully compared to the current case.
Surpassed means exceeded in quality; legal analogy compares similarity, not making judgments about which case is stronger.
Refuted means proven wrong; an analogous precedent supports the legal team's argument, not refutes it.
Nullified means made void or invalid; drawing on an analogous precedent strengthens the argument, not nullifies it.
Abrogated means officially annulled; an analogous precedent remains relevant and applicable to the current case.

sentenceSets.sentence: The economist noted that the financial crisis of 2008 was analogous to the Great Depression in its causes and consequences, though the details differed.

answerChoices.reasoning: Identical means exactly the same; while analogous, the sentence explicitly notes that details differed between the two crises.
More severe indicates greater intensity; an analogy compares similarities, not making value judgments about severity.
Caused means produced or brought about; while analogous crises may share causes, one did not cause the other.
Preceded means came before; while the Depression preceded 2008, the analogy compares similarities, not temporal sequence.
Derived means originating from; while there might be connections, an analogy emphasizes similarity of structure and causes.
Opposite means contrary; comparing causes and consequences suggests similarity, not opposition.
Unrelated means having no connection; noting analogous causes and consequences demonstrates connection.
Inferior means lower in quality or importance; an analogy compares structural similarities, not making quality judgments.
Contradicted means opposed; noting shared causes and consequences indicates confirmation of similarities, not contradiction.
Distinct means separate or different; an analogy specifically highlights important similarities despite differences in details.
Superseding means replacing or surpassing; an analogy compares two phenomena without claiming one supersedes the other.
